purpose: Requirements closed as far as the artifacts of their own gate allow, each naming the gate or slice that completes them. tools/partial_closures.py fails the build on an entry with no completer, an unknown completer, a completer that has landed while the entry is still open, or a completer that has been moved LATER without a recorded reason.

partial_closures.why: The preview names line prices, modifiers, tax, fees and discounts. Tax resolves to config.configuration_version under category 'tax' and a discount to config.policy under category 'discount'; both are configured, non-zero and exercised. A FEE has no configuration heading before FR-CFG-001C, so ordering.charge_rule can hold one and nothing at this gate creates one. The total is a sum over the components that exist and carries no zero literal for the absent kind.

completer_moved.why: Refined from the gate M4 to the slice that genuinely completes it. Moved EARLIER: M4-A is the first slice at which this can be closed, and it is closed there. The gate was named at M3 because M4 had no slice shape yet; it does now.

partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: Migration 0019 creates billing.service_charge_setting, which points at an approved config.configuration_version of category 'service' — FR-CFG-001C's heading, and the configured source the 'fee' charge kind has never had. billing.issue_bill() computes the fee at stage 4 on the base the setting says it applies to, refuses to charge a fee on itself, and records the rate, the base, the rounding mode and the configuration id in the component's basis. tests/m4a recomputes all four components in Python from the configured rates and requires the database to match, and asserts from the catalog that the fee component names a configuration version of category 'service' rather than a constant. There is still no fee column and no fee literal anywhere.

partial_closures.why: Whether a discount applies before or after tax is a bill-calculation decision. At M3-A both are computed on the line subtotal, which is the only reading that does not pre-empt FR-BIL-005.

completer_moved.why: Refined from the gate M4 to the slice that genuinely completes it. Moved EARLIER: M4-A is the first slice at which this can be closed, and it is closed there. The gate was named at M3 because M4 had no slice shape yet; it does now.

partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: billing.issue_bill() states the four stages explicitly and records each component's stage in its basis: item subtotal, discount on the subtotal, TAX ON THE DISCOUNTED SUBTOTAL, then the service charge on its configured base. Taxing first would charge tax on money nobody was asked for, and the two readings round differently — so the reading is stated, recorded per component, and carried by a persisted calculation version. tests/m4a asserts the tax component's recorded base equals the subtotal less the discount, and that the stages come back in that order.

partial_closures.why: Item, modifier, discount, tax and total snapshots persist at acceptance with the locale. The fee snapshot persists the moment a fee component exists, and no configured source produces one before M4.

completer_moved.why: Refined from the gate M4 to the slice that genuinely completes it. Moved EARLIER: M4-A is the first slice at which this can be closed, and it is closed there. The gate was named at M3 because M4 had no slice shape yet; it does now.

partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: The fee is a bill component like any other and carries the same snapshot every other component does: source_kind 'service_configuration', the id of the approved configuration version it was read from, and a basis recording the percentage, the rounding mode, the base it was computed on and which kinds it applied to. The whole is in the ledger event that produced the projection, so a rebuild reproduces it. tests/m4a joins the component to config.configuration_version and requires the category to be 'service'.

partial_closures.why: A draft cart creates no order, no ledger event and no charge component, and a cart with an order against it is frozen. That a draft creates no FINANCIAL obligation is re-proved once checks and payments exist; the requirements register already dual-gates this row at M4.

completer_moved.why: Refined from the gate M4 to the slice that genuinely completes it. Moved EARLIER: M4-A is the first slice at which this can be closed, and it is closed there. The gate was named at M3 because M4 had no slice shape yet; it does now.

partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: A draft cart still creates no order and no ledger event, and now demonstrably no financial obligation either: billing.check_allocation is written only by billing.allocate_to_check(), which resolves the ORDER behind a line and refuses ALLOCATION_ORDER_NOT_BILLABLE for anything the house has not accepted. There is no path from a cart to a check, a bill or a charge component, and the application role holds no write grant on the bill projection at all. tests/m4a submits an order and leaves it unaccepted, then requires the allocation to be refused by name.

partial_closures.why: Availability, hours, channel and quantity are revalidated at submission. Capacity is the fifth dimension the requirement names and it means station workload, which needs the stations and their thresholds that FR-FUL-013 builds at M3-B.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: ordering.revalidate_cart() gained a fifth leg at M3-B reading fulfillment.capacity_pressure(), which compares each station's live ticket count against its configured concurrent_ticket_threshold and reports the outlet's configured capacity_response. A service policy stating neither is refused, not defaulted. tests/m3b loads a station past its threshold and requires the submission to be blocked under a throttling policy and to proceed under a promise-time policy.

partial_closures.why: Add-on orders in one session are distinct aggregates with independent timestamps and independent ledgers, which is proved here. That their FULFILLMENT is independent needs tickets, which are M3-B.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: Tickets belong to an ORDER, and an add-on is a different order, so independent fulfillment came out of the model rather than being added to it. tests/m3b places a second order on one occupancy and requires disjoint ticket sets, independent state machines and independent timings.

partial_closures.why: Amendment emits an explicit event retaining before and after, and the window is enforced from the ordering policy. The policy can only speak in commercial states at this gate: 'after preparation has begun' is a ticket state and tickets are M3-B.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: ordering.amend_order_line() was replaced at M3-B (CREATE OR REPLACE; 0010 is checksum-locked) to refuse when any ticket for the order has left queued, acknowledged or held. The commercial state alone was never enough: an order can sit in a state the ordering policy permits while a station is already cooking it.
partial_closures.completer_aspect: the ticket state a station records as it works, which fulfillment keeps in the cloud and which the amendment refusal reads. FR-FUL-003's open half is serving that same state to a screen FROM THE OUTLET NODE, and this closure does not rest on where the screen gets it: an order whose ticket has left queued is un-amendable whether or not anybody is looking at a KDS.

partial_closures.aspect: payment dimension of the cancellation policy
partial_closures.why: Cancellation resolves by state, channel and reason. The payment dimension needs payments to exist; the requirements register already dual-gates this row at M4.

completer_moved.why: MOVED LATER, from M4 to M4-B. The clause is 'apply the cancellation policy by state, channel, reason, PAYMENT and preparation progress'. M4-A takes no payment, so the payment dimension has no value to read and a control planted against it would assert over an empty set — the same defect this entry was opened to avoid at M3-A. M4-B captures payment and is the first slice at which 'this order was paid, so this cancellation is refused' can be made false.

partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: Migration 0025 replaces ordering.cancel_order(). State, channel, reason and preparation progress have decided since M3-A; payment is the fifth and could not be applied to an empty set. A paid order is cancellable only where the outlet's cancellation policy says paid_orders_cancellable, because cancelling an order somebody paid for without returning the money is the failure mode and the refund is FR-PAY-009's separate authorized act rather than a side effect of pressing cancel. Whether the order was paid is recorded on the event as well as consulted, so the decision is answerable afterwards.

partial_closures.why: An authorized void after acceptance records its reason and an immutable audit row. 'For an unpaid order' cannot be falsified at M3-A because no payment artifact exists to make it false, so the precondition is asserted against an empty set and must be re-proved at M4.

completer_moved.why: MOVED LATER, from M4 to M4-B. The clause is an authorized void 'for an UNPAID order'. The completer named at M3-A was FR-BIL-014, which is tip separation and closes nothing here; it is corrected to FR-BIL-008, whose settled bill balance is what makes an order paid.

partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: Migration 0025 replaces ordering.void_order(). 'For an unpaid order' is now a condition that can be false: payments.order_is_paid() decides it, and tests/m4b pays an order in full and requires the void to be refused with VOID_OF_PAID_ORDER. partial_closures.aspect: budgets calibrated against the runner, not against wall clock alone
partial_closures.why:
The budgets are real and they are measured in a real browser under a real throttle, which is what FR-UX-012 asks for. What they cannot currently do is tell a slow ARTIFACT from a starved RUNNER, and on Windows that has now cost three false reds. First contentful paint on the Windows runner has been measured at 1332ms, 1912ms, 2188ms, 5448ms and 21432ms against a 2500ms budget — and the 21432ms and the 1912ms are the SAME COMMIT, re-run, with a byte-identical bundle. An eleven-fold spread on identical bytes is not a property of the artifact.

M3-C named the honest fix and deferred it on one data point; it has recurred twice since, so the deferral is due rather than renewable. The fix is NOT a larger number: a budget adjusted to accommodate a flake stops being a budget, and every red it reports afterwards is worth less. It is to measure a REFERENCE OPERATION in the same run — something whose cost is known and which depends on the machine rather than on this surface — and express the budget relative to it, so a run in which everything is ten times slower is reported as a starved runner and a run in which only the surface is slower is reported as a regression. The absolute numbers stay exactly where they are.

M4-A because it is the next slice, and because leaving it open through another gate is what turned one observation into three.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: tests/m2c/render_probe.mjs measures a reference operation — a fixed compute loop, median of five, on about:blank under the same CPU throttle — immediately before the timed load, and reports it as referenceMs. verify_m2c computes a factor against a recorded baseline and expresses every interaction budget relative to it, so a run where everything is ten times slower reads as a starved runner (PERFORMANCE_NOT_MEASURABLE) and a run where only the surface is slower reads as a regression (PERFORMANCE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED). THE ABSOLUTE NUMBERS DID NOT MOVE. Landed at f27761f as the calibration M3 deferred on a single data point and then saw recur twice.

partial_closures.why: Split out of the M3-C entry, which named 'bill, payment, tip, outage and sync producers' as one aspect and said outage and sync were 'recorded separately'. An aspect that spans M4 and M5a can close at neither, so the claim would have kept the entry open past both. notify.catalog_event carries both kinds with has_producer = false and notify.emit() refuses them by name, so nothing pretends to raise one in the meantime.

partial_closures.aspect: acceptance on a verified payment outcome
partial_closures.why: An order configured for payment-dependent acceptance is accepted ONLY after a verified payment outcome. M4-A supplies everything except the verification: ordering.acceptance_mode carries 'payment_dependent', ordering.submit_order() auto-accepts only 'automatic' so such an order stays submitted, and migration 0020 makes ordering.accept_order() refuse it by name with ACCEPTANCE_AWAITS_PAYMENT_VERIFICATION. That is the fail-closed half and it is the correct behaviour of the finished system too. What is missing is a verified outcome to consult and a path that consults it, and 'verified' is M4-B's word.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: Migration 0025 replaces ordering.accept_order(). A payment-dependent order is accepted only when payments.order_is_paid() is true, and VERIFIED means four things that are already true by constraint before that function is reached: the payment came through an adapter whose mode is DERIVED FROM ITS PROVIDER by CHECK, so no direct-provider adapter can be behind it; its outcome is 'approved' in a column typed payments.live_outcome, a type no simulator can produce a value of and to which no cast exists; for a proof-based provider a named person on their own live session recorded what they saw in the provider's application, all four fields required together; and the money reached the BILL BALANCE as its own allocation row, which payments.assert_allocation_is_earned() refuses to write unless the first three hold. The refusal 0020 introduced is unchanged and remains the answer for an unpaid order. tests/m4b proves a tip of the full amount does not buy acceptance, and that the acceptance mode is recorded on the event so an order accepted because it was paid for is distinguishable afterwards. 0025 also opens billing.allocate_to_check() to a SUBMITTED order at an outlet whose policy is payment_dependent, because otherwise the requirement is circular: nothing in that mode could be billed, so nothing could be paid for, so nothing could be accepted.

partial_closures.why: Finalization requires a settled balance or an authorized disposition. M4-A takes no payment, so the disposition branch is the only reachable one and it is fully proved: comped, written off and transferred, each with an override naming two people and a reason. The settled-by-payment branch is unreachable until there is a tender, so billing.outstanding_balance() subtracts dispositions and nothing else. M4-B adds the tender to that subtraction.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: Migration 0025 replaces billing.outstanding_balance(). It subtracts authorized dispositions AND bill-balance allocations net of reversals, so a bill paid in full is settled and billing.finalize_bill() lets it close. What it still does not read is billing.tip, and tests/m4a's derivation over every balance function in the catalog is unchanged and still passes — the function ceased to be blind to money without becoming able to see a tip. The M4-B suite found the gap by paying a bill exactly and finding the whole amount still owed.

partial_closures.why: Bill balance, service charge, tax, tip and total tendered are separate values and separate records. Four of the five exist and are proved separate — the balance and its components on billing.bill, the tip in its own table with no column anywhere that could hold one and no balance function that reads one. TOTAL TENDERED has no record because nothing is tendered at this gate, and a zero column standing in for it would be the vacuity this project has caught three times.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: payments.payment carries tendered_minor and change_minor as stored columns and payments.allocation carries the bill-balance and tip figures as separate rows, so all five of FR-BIL-014's values are separate records: balance and components on billing.bill, tip in billing.tip, and total tendered here. tests/m4b recomputes the change in Python from the tender and what was owed and requires the database to match, scans all three surface bundles for arithmetic on a tendered amount and finds none, and proves the allocations do not follow the bill by reissuing it and requiring the figures to be unchanged.

partial_closures.why: Tip refunds, reversals and corrections are separate auditable records linked to the original tip. billing.tip_correction carries all three kinds, is append-only by trigger and by grant, names the override and the reason, and tests/m4a proves a reversal moves no balance. What a refund cannot yet do is return money, because there is no provider and nothing was taken; the RECORD is complete and the movement is M4-B's.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: payments.reversal reverses ONE allocation, so a tip payment is refunded without touching the bill payment and the other way round — which is what 'separate linked reversal records' needs in order to be expressible. It carries the reason code, the approval threshold read from config.policy, and an override whose approver is derived from the approving session. tests/m4b reverses a tip and a bill payment on one payment and proves each moved only its own figure. What a refund still cannot do is push money back through a provider, because there is no provider: the RECORD is complete and the remittance is outside Phase 1, which the M4-C entry records.

partial_closures.why: The translated bill summary renders on the customer surface in all three launch locales, with the optional tip box after or beside it and never inside it — measured in Chromium as DOM containment and as the two rectangles the layout produced. What is not here is the printed artifact: paper, the fiscal adapter and the receipt are M4-C, and a bill on a screen and a bill on paper are the same document rendered by different means.

M4-A built the tax, service-charge and tip halves of the guided setup and used FR-CFG-001C as the completer of FR-ORD-003's fee component and FR-ORD-005's fee snapshot. Its fourth clause — the permitted PAYMENT METHODS, and the requirement that all of them drive a real bill — could not exist before payments did, and no entry recorded that. This entry is that record, written at M4-B and backdated to the slice where the gap opened, and it is the case that motivated PARTIAL_CLOSURE_COMPLETER_INCOMPLETE.
partial_closures.closed_by_evidence: Migration 0025 adds payments.install_adapters_from_configuration(), which reads the approved configuration version of category 'payment_method' and builds the adapter registry from it. payments.create_intent() then takes an intent's permitted providers from the registry, and one of them settles a real bill — so the chain from setup to money is one tests/m4b walks rather than a claim. The payload cannot say whether an adapter is SIMULATED: that is derived from the provider by CHECK, so a configuration file is not a route to NC-M4-003.

partial_closures.why: Bills, payments, tips and cash movements are append-only or reversal-based with no destructive correction: billing.bill_event and payments.payment_event are append-only by trigger and by grant, their projections are written only by a fold, billing.tip_correction and payments.reversal are separate linked records, and cash.movement and cash.shift_transition refuse UPDATE and DELETE. RECEIPTS are the one artifact the requirement names that does not exist yet; they are M4-C's, and no zero-row table stands in for them.

partial_closures.aspect: node connectivity, sync lag and printer status
partial_closures.why: Health reports the ACTIVE payment adapters truthfully, and an advertised adapter that cannot settle makes readiness unhealthy — tests/m4b activates a simulated adapter and requires a 503. The other three things FR-INT-011 names have nothing behind them at this gate: the outlet node and synchronization lag are M5a's and the printer is M4-C's. M1-D's rule is that a deployment advertises what it HAS, so none is reported. A health endpoint calling a printer healthy because no printer exists would be the most expensive kind of true statement.

partial_closures.aspect: cash service through a staged outage
partial_closures.why: Proved STRUCTURALLY and not behaviourally, and the structural half is the stronger claim. tests/m4b derives the transitive closure of every function reachable from the cash, terminal-recording and proof-confirmation entry points from the catalog, defines 'outbound' by CAPABILITY — an untrusted language, a foreign table, a non-core extension, or a write to the table that records an adapter call — and requires the intersection to be empty; it then plants an adapter call on the cash path and requires the check to go red. Staging one outage would prove the path survived THAT outage; this proves it survives every outage. What is missing is the behavioural half, which needs an outlet node to switch off. DISTINCT FROM FR-FUL-001's routing-during-an-outage entry, which is about work reaching a station while the node is isolated: this one is about money being taken while it is, and M5a discharges neither by discharging the other.

A refund is a complete, authorized, linked RECORD: it names one allocation, its reason code, the approval its amount required and the override that gave it, and payments.assert_reversal_is_authorized() refuses one whose approval belongs to somebody else or to a different refund. What it cannot do is move money back to a card or a wallet, because no provider is contracted — FR-PAY-015 keeps the direct APIs simulated. Cash refunds are complete today: they are a movement out of the drawer.

partial_closures.aspect: every landed requirement audited, not only named completers
partial_closures.why: PARTIAL_CLOSURE_COMPLETER_INCOMPLETE checks that no closed entry rests on a requirement carrying an open entry of its own, and the rule states its own boundary: it checks NAMED COMPLETERS, not every requirement whose gate has landed. A requirement that is partly built and that no entry points at is still invisible. The larger audit — every landed requirement either delivered in full or carrying an entry — is the correct rule in general and is deliberately not this slice's: it would expand the highest-consequence slice in the project while payment capture was being written, which is how a money defect slips through while everyone is reading a register. It comes due at M4-C, where a gate is closing rather than where money is being taken.

gate_decomposition.note:
M4's split into slices A, B and C is THIS REPOSITORY'S DECOMPOSITION, not the pinned package's. The package defines M4 as one gate — 'POS, billing and settlement', 55 requirements, one exit criterion — and names no slices. M1, M2 and M3 were decomposed the same way and for the same reason: a gate of that size is not reviewable as one change. A reviewer should meet this as a stated decision rather than infer it from slice names that do not appear in the pinned artifact.

It matters here because tools/partial_closures.py derives landing from the filesystem: tests/m4a lands both M4-A and M4, so an entry naming the bare gate M4 comes due on the FIRST slice of that gate. Thirteen entries named M4 because that was the most precise thing sayable at M3, before the slice shape existed. They were re-pointed at M4-A to the slice that genuinely completes each, and every one that moved LATER carries its reason in the entry.

slices.M4-B: payment capture, provider integration, verification, reconciliation and cash shifts
